clue.text: Fast to make a point, thinkers urge change

indicators.note: to change these words is to rework their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Intellectuals are urged to change their ways, with a fast mentioned at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is the noun, a period without food; the whole first part of the clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunger strike is a refusal of food undertaken as a protest, a fast with a political purpose.

clue.text: Release snake to bite off relative's foot

indicators.note: the snake bites something off, so a letter is removed from the relative
the foot of a down word is its last letter, the letter bitten off

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A snake is freed to bite off the foot of a family member, a gruesome little scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the foot is the last letter; the snake comes after the trimmed relative though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclasp is to undo a grip or fastening and so let something go free.

clue.text: I'm surprised about order to attempt mathematical discipline

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about, or around, the order

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
to try is to attempt

explanation.surface: Someone expresses surprise at being told to try a branch of maths.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour, so 'order' here is not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the branch of mathematics studying shapes, lines and angles.

clue.text: Trump violent? So it's said

indicators.note: signals that the word for violent is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: rough means violent

explanation.surface: Reads as a comment on a famous politician's temper, attributed to hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' is not the politician but the card-game verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games to ruff is to play a trump card on a trick when unable to follow suit.

clue.text: What cannibals do for old left-wingers' medications

indicators.note: one thing put in for, or instead of, another signals a replacement

parts.note: Trots is a nickname for Trotskyists, far-left activists
cannibals eat men

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what cannibals would do with the medicines of aged leftists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link but signals swapping one piece in for another; 'old' is the piece that leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatments are remedies or medical care given for an illness, so medications fit as a plural noun.

clue.text: Confirm selection, barely winking

indicators.note: taking the word barely, stripped of its outside letters, leaves just its core

explanation.surface: Someone confirms a choice with the faintest of winks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' strips the outside letters W and G from winking.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink in is to finalise something pencilled, such as a team selection, by writing it in ink.

clue.text: Look at upper limit one German is holding up

indicators.note: the German word holds the limit inside it

parts.note: eine is German for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the upper limit

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a ceiling figure that a German is propping up.
explanation.walkthrough: The German word is the feminine form of one, not the more familiar masculine form.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect it closely, to look at it carefully.

clue.text: Way to suggest Rod races and goes unprecedentedly fast

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: BREAK (an anagram signal) applied to S plus A RECORD gives the letters of Rod races

explanation.surface: Someone named Rod races and sets a new speed record.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, taken as an instruction, rearranges S A RECORD into ROD RACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking a record means beating the best previous performance, so going faster than anyone has before.

clue.text: He may start fast rowers featured by What Crew? unexpectedly

indicators.note: the rowers appear inside, featured by, the jumbled words
the letters fall in an unexpected order

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing crew features in a puzzled question about who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The rowers land inside the jumbled letters, splitting them after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A Weight Watcher is a dieter in that slimming programme, someone who may begin a diet by fasting.

clue.text: Deciding heat for cafe demolition

indicators.note: the words are knocked down and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a hot argument over knocking down a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' means a round of a race, not warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A race-off is an extra race held to settle a tie, a deciding round in a competition.

clue.text: Free at last, daleks devastated Lake District attraction

indicators.note: take only the final letter of the word free
the letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Escaped Daleks, the Doctor Who villains, wreck a beauty spot in Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a national park in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eskdale is a scenic valley in the Lake District, popular with walkers and visitors.

clue.text: Native American losing his head fast

indicators.note: the Native American loses a letter, which is taken out

parts.note: an Apache is a member of a Native American people

indicators.note: the head of his is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Native American loses his head quickly, a grim little tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The H that APACHE loses is the head of 'his', not of APACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly, at a rapid speed.

clue.text: Fast and ingenious protecting rank

indicators.note: the words protect, or enclose, the answer within them

explanation.surface: Praise for a quick and clever bodyguard of some rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing means status or position in a hierarchy, the same as rank.

clue.text: Roquefort, typically scandalously unbelieved

indicators.note: the letters behave scandalously and get out of order

explanation.surface: A cheese described in disbelief, as if caught in a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquefort is a classic blue cheese, marbled with mould, so it is an example of the type.

clue.text: Pursued with leg broken very fast indeed

indicators.note: the leg is broken, and its letters are mixed into the others

explanation.surface: Someone was chased and broke a leg while running very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' here means firmly fixed, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superglued is stuck firmly in place, held fast by strong adhesive.

clue.text: Advanced fast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: loaned, as money advanced
second meaning: the forty days of Christian fasting before Easter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced' looks like a description of speed next to fast; it means loaned.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of lend, and also the Christian season of abstinence before Easter.

clue.text: Bread and tea with songwriter Smith

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Patti Smith is an American singer-songwriter

explanation.surface: A menu of bread and tea with a famous singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is a flat unleavened bread from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Band move fast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the Canadian rock group

explanation.definitionFit: Rush is the name of a well-known Canadian rock trio, and also a verb meaning to hurry.

clue.text: Little guys I avoid — Rishi mad with some other politicians

indicators.note: the letter I is avoided, left out of the name
the remaining letters go mad and change order

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament, politicians other than the named prime minister

explanation.surface: Someone shuns the former prime minister Rishi Sunak, who has gone mad among his colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an I from RISHI and rearrange to get SHRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimps is informal for small people, a jokey term for anyone diminutive.

clue.text: Figures in 3 lesson get head tangling with parent

indicators.note: the words become tangled, their letters mixed together

explanation.surface: A pupil gets in a muddle with a parent over homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 points to 3-down, GEOMETRY, so the definition is shapes studied in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentahedra are solid shapes with five faces, studied in a geometry class.

clue.text: A couple of parties, the second about an hour, for Indian interpreter

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the second party goes about, around, the hour

parts.note: a bash is a party, the second of the couple
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the parties an interpreter attends.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an old Anglo-Indian word, so it is likely to be unfamiliar and needs building from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dobhash was an interpreter in colonial India, from a word meaning two languages.

clue.text: President created uproar with shag on floor

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into uproar and disorder

explanation.surface: A president causes a scandal with something risqué happening on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shag' means a thick-piled rug, not the rude British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor covered in shag-pile rug is carpeted.

clue.text: Fast guy from Motorhead skinning bears for children

indicators.note: skinning removes the outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: teddies are toy bears for children

explanation.surface: A heavy-metal musician strips the fur from children's toy bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast Eddie Clarke was guitarist of the rock band Motörhead; the nickname is the clue's joke.

clue.text: Bar one beginning to cut some hair

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing a kind of hair

parts.note: a pub is a bar
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the first letter of the word cut

explanation.surface: A pub announces it will start offering haircuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubic hair grows in the groin, a particular kind of body hair.

clue.text: Bottoms of seats clean, characteristic of foreign train service

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of each word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Clean seats on a train are typical of a foreign rail operator.
explanation.definitionFit: SNCF is the French national railway company, a train operator abroad.

clue.text: Fast in the daytime for a period, Adam ran off

definitions.text: Fast in the daytime for a period

indicators.note: the words go off, out of their order

explanation.surface: Adam left during a daytime fast that lasted a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month when believers abstain from food from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Fast one could be dangerous

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A speeding car or person might be a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not safe is risky or hazardous, the same as dangerous.

clue.text: Budgie-smugglers on staircase as fast as possible

parts.note: Australian slang for tight swimming trunks, the brand name Speedo
a flight is a staircase

explanation.surface: A man in skimpy trunks on the stairs is rushing.
explanation.walkthrough: Speedos are tight men's swim briefs; budgie-smugglers is the jokey Australian name for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The speed of light is the universe's speed limit, nothing travels faster.
